nom: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Melt-in Milk Body & Face Sunscreen Lotion SPF 100

segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin describe the formula as helpful and glowing, though one specifically warns that people with normal or oily skin likely won't like how it sits on top rather than sinking in.
segments.oily: Reviewers are split: one with oily skin found it made her skin look more oily, while another with combination, acne-prone, oily-t-zone skin kept using it without singling out oiliness as a problem.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin, some also describing it as sensitive or acne-prone, report mixed results, from clogged pores and t-zone breakouts to no issues at all depending on the reviewer.
segments.sensitive: Many reviewers with sensitive skin, including several with rosacea, lupus or MCAS, say this is one of the few sunscreens that doesn't trigger their reactions or breakouts, though a couple of self-described sensitive-skin reviewers still found it irritating, drying or breakout-inducing.

concerns.dehydration: Reviewers with dry skin describe the lotion as glowing and moisturizing, feeling like an added layer of hydration rather than a typical sunscreen.
concerns.redness: Reviewers with rosacea, lupus or generally redness-prone sensitive skin report this sunscreen is one of the few that doesn't trigger flare-ups or worsen their redness, though one rosacea reviewer says it still triggered breakouts and excessive pilling in her t-zone.
concerns.blemishes: Most acne-prone reviewers, including several with sensitive or hormonal-acne-prone skin, report the sunscreen does not cause breakouts, though one reviewer with rosacea and combination skin says it triggered t-zone breakouts and she had to stop using it on her face.
concerns.oiliness: One reviewer with oily skin found it made her skin noticeably more oily, though a reviewer with combination, oily-t-zone, acne-prone skin kept using it without that becoming a dealbreaker.

aspects.libelle: Stings or burns badly if it gets near or into the eyes
Melts in with no white cast, even on deep or brown skin tones
Can pill or clump when layered with makeup or other products
Reliable high-SPF protection, no burns even after hours in the sun
Can stain clothing with bright yellow marks

extraits.texte: I have severely dry skin so this formula is helpful towards that. Anyone with normal or oily skin wont like this though. Doesnt sink into skin. Cant use under makeup. Stings the eyes for the entire day. Smells like a typical sunscreen. I prefer the formulations ive gotten off of yesstyle so much more.

I bought this because I have rosacea and needed a higher spf but hated that other spfs smelled and felt like your typical sunscreen. The feel of this is super smooth and my face felt hydrated afterwards. However my skin pilled SOOOOOOO much. No matter what i did or how I changed the amount I put on. It also triggered breakouts for me in my t zone (I have combination skin). Since stopping it, I've realized a lot less flare ups. But as a sunscreen itself, it does its job.
i liked it, its a very good product, goes smooth on the skin but, since i have oily skin this product wasn't on of my favorites since it made my skin more oily

okay this sunscreen is actually really good! it doesnt break me out(which my skin is super sensitive to break outs and redness), gives me a slight glow, and obviously its spf 100 which is lovely for my fair skin. however, i play tennis a lot and even when im out for like 5 minutes and this is on my face i sweat like CRAZY even though im not even hot or tired or any of that. and when i actually do get hot and work out for a long time dear lord it looks like i just went on a 5k marathon through death valley. it doesnt bug me that much cause its protecting my skin but it is sorta annoying. also omg for the love of god do NOT get this anywhere near your eyes. i got this near my eyes and no matter how much i washed them or wiped my eyes my eyes were burning for 3+ hours. literally. they were watering so bad and i was blinking every millisecond and couldnt barely do anything. other than that its a really solid sunscreen if one you dont put it near your eyes and two you dont mind sweating(if youre being active/doing sports).

Went to Florida for a week and was looking for something to protect me while I was in the sun all day, everyday. It felt nice and there wasn't any white cast or stinging. I have hormonal-acne prone skin that's sensitive and didn't have any troubles with it. The only trouble I seemed to have with it was using it around my eyes. After it set, I rubbed my eyes and it stung my eyes. It lasted for a while afterwards, so I would be careful with usage around the area and not to rub anywhere near your eyes. Other than that, it helped me from getting super sunburnt. Will purchase next vacation!
I have combination + sensitive skin & my forehead clogs easily, this sunscreen blends into the skin so well, leaves the skin nice & glowy & doesn't irritate or clog my pores. as a esthi I APPROVE

extraits.titre: Combo, Acne-Prone, 20-something Girl Approved (and her dad)
extraits.texte: I love this sunscreen! I have used the SPF 60 version for a couple of years and then a year ago I decided to give this SPF 100 a shot to see if I liked it (and benefit from higher SPF!) or whether I should stick to the SPF 60. I have combo, acne-prone skin with an oily T-zone, an oil slick of a nose, and my under eyes have started to get drier. I'd describe the texture as a thick lotion so it works amazing during the winter months as a moisturizer too, but it's not too thick for the summer months and I don't find it to be too shiny! I find this version to be a little tackier and oddly a little less shiny (by like, a hair) than the SPF 60 so I loooovvee using this under makeup on a day when I'm spending time outside but need makeup on my face! The tackiness makes it so the sunscreen dries down faster than the 60 SPF had and I can place makeup in the areas I wanted. I really liked that because I felt like when I used eyeshadow there was no danger of it sliding where I hadn't placed it -- it just stuck to the right spot. I've never used this under foundation, however, because when I'm using this I'm gonna be outside and not really wanting foundation to potentially mess up my sun protection. My 62 yr old dad also loves this, although he loves Bondi Sands SPF more probably because that one feels even more moisturizing than this. My only con is that when I reapply this, I personally have to wash off the first layer and then reapply -- sometimes it feels like the reapplication layer
